title: Setting the Load Down
logline: Estate workers carry tea-leaf baskets down a mountain path all morning, and the moment each basket reaches the weighing shed and comes off a back, something visibly changes in the body underneath it.
human_question: What does relief actually look like on a body, and how much of goodness might be exactly that?

premise.story: A day of leaf-plucking and carrying on a hill-country tea estate, from the first climb of the morning to the last basket weighed in.
premise.place: Steep tea rows and a mountain path, cool air, a weighing shed at the bottom of the slope.
premise.experience: The rhythm of ascent and descent, the accumulating weight, and the exact moment of setting it down.

concept_links.why: Lightness is pictured as putting down a load carried from far away, and the whole pair of qualities describes real ease in body as well as mind [C023-P:L137].
Only the factors a moment's work actually requires arise with it; effort itself is neither good nor bad, entirely coloured by what it serves [C019-P:L49; C019-P:L61-L63].

what_camera_could_observe: Baskets going up the slope empty at dawn
The climb, the picking, the weight accumulating on backs
The walk down and the weighing
Workers' shoulders and breathing before and immediately after the basket comes off
what_must_be_real: The workers' actual wages, conditions and choices about this work. No staged relief or performed exhaustion.

possible_arc.opening: Empty baskets climbing the slope at first light.
possible_arc.turn: The long carry through heat and fatigue.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever the workers actually say about the work, the weight, and the relief, if they say anything at all.

requirements: An active tea estate willing to allow filming of real pickers over a working day
Honest access to conditions and pay, not only the picturesque parts of the process
Workers' full consent to be filmed and interviewed

suggestions.name: Hatton-Dickoya tea estate region
suggestions.why: A well-known, long-established tea-growing area with active estates and pluckers.
suggestions.verify: No specific estate or workers have been identified or confirmed.

risks: Aestheticising real economic hardship as a metaphor
drop_if: No estate or workers are willing to be filmed honestly, including about conditions and pay, not only the visual rhythm of the work

connections.note: Both use a real, physical process as the direct image of a beautiful factor: lightness here, softness there.
Both are physically demanding group or individual labour used to show what goodness's ease and coordination can look like in the body.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
